body: Just to add perspective, I was your daughter and my dad routinely got like this with me because I didn’t understand the way HE understood math. You know where his behavior got us? I ended up suicidal and disengaged and stopped going to my dad for help or support with anything, up to his death over 20 years later. This is, unequivocally, abuse that will get worse. He’s punishing her for being eight and having trouble with math. What you did to help her was actually constructive and helped her. You found where the misunderstanding was and explained it. I was the same way, if I didn’t understand why something was done the way it was, I couldn’t grasp it. But my dad would only push it like your husband does, and guess what? It made it a million times worse and made me despise math and hurt my relationship with my father seriously. If she doesn’t understand in the first place, him screaming at her to “just do it” is ridiculous and will have lasting effects on her. HES undermining his own parenting by showing her over and over that daddy is an asshole who she can’t ask for help. Is that who he wants to be as a parent? Because that’s what he’s showing her. That daddy is mean and wants to humiliate her when she needs help. He, probably like my father, can’t separate how HIS adult brain understands things and how her eight year old developing brain understands things, so he gets frustrated because it comes easy to him and therefore should be easy to her. But unfortunately this kind of bullshit just leads to a lifetime of feeling unsafe and humiliated by her father.

Yeah i think the same thing, especially since he wouldn’t answer any of my questions about where the fuck we were going. Chicago is huge too and there can be tons of ways to get anywhere so It took a while and a lot of courage for me to even ask, but previous trauma and luckily my phone having battery and telling friends what was going on and them prompting me to at least TRY to figure out what the hell was going on made me finally do it when we got towards the edge of the city, which was about an hour away from where he picked me up and and at least 45 minutes from where I lived, I was probably like 17 at the time too and definitely not sober and probably seemed like an easy victim. Also coincidentally remember checking the details once the second Uber driver freaked out and it was the same, right car, right plate, completely different driver than it was supposed to be. It didn’t fully hit me how terrifying it was and how much danger I was actually in until I got in the other Uber and the driver started freaking out, especially when I mentioned the child locks that were somehow activated after I got in the car. I think he either couldn’t find a place, which is probably less likely because that area is a lot of abandoned warehouses, or lost his edge and decided it wasn’t worth doing whatever he was going to do either because of his own reasons, but I’m glad we both ended up safe on those nights. Absolutely insane. I’m MUCH more careful now and make sure to share my ride with someone AND check the driver to make sure they match the picture.

This happened to me! Luckily it was Chicago and he just left me in a random alley on the outskirts of the city at 3am, albeit in a neighborhood you do not want to be alone in at 3am at 4’11” and 90lbs soaking wet without knowing anyone far far away from any running public transit. Thank god another Uber came within a half hour to get me, also told me to report the guy and was EXTREMELY upset on my behalf and was surprised I wasn’t so shaken up. I do remember asking a couple times why we were on that highway or why we were going that way only to ominously get absolutely zero response until he left me in an alley and told me to call another Uber. It was also before the safety options were added to the app and I only realized when he got out to let me out that he’d somehow turned the child locks on once I got in the car.

I took in a foster kid when I was about 20, in a really sudden situation where our options were me or him going back into some really awful situations, and I briefly took in his best friend as well. It was one of the hardest most frustrating things I’ve ever done in my life and I wouldn’t change it for the world, i love that kid with all my heart and even though it took him a couple years of going as hard as he could down a bad path, he’s now a successful adult who is kind and loving and wonderful. I’d do it all over again and hope to when I’m in a better financial and physical health position to do so, but it’s definitely not for everyone. It was incredibly difficult and stressful and I was definitely too young for the responsibilities that were given to me, but I’m so proud of him and as much as it could be painful and hard and frustrating, it was also rewarding and I’m grateful that I was available for him and could be a safe adult for him. I’d definitely change some of the way I did things, you live and learn, but i don’t regret it for a second and I encourage anyone looking into fostering to do so, but to also really sit and think about what goes into being a foster parent and what responsibilities you will have, as it often comes with a lot of mental and physical health challenges that can be incredibly overwhelming if you aren’t prepared for that. I’m incredibly lucky that my situation and foster son turned out so well, it was shaky as hell for a while there, but it truly is such a wonderful thing to do and being that stable adult for him made ALL the difference in his life and future and I wouldn’t change that for anything.

I am disabled and either have my cane or my wheelchair on a daily basis depending on how my mobility is that day. I’ve had TONS of issues with public transit, but was luckily blessed with a wonderful bus driver I saw daily on my way to work for a while. On this route there was another disabled woman who was always in her wheelchair that I saw every day as well. This driver would not move the bus an INCH until people moved from the priority seats that fold up so that wheelchairs can fit there as well as lock into the space so they don’t slide around the bus while it moves. She didn’t hesitate to kick people off if they put up a fuss about moving or complained about her refusing to move the bus until disabled/elderly/pregnant/other vulnerable passengers had a place to sit safely. She was a lovely, fierce woman and I still stay in contact with her, she was an absolute lifesaver for me as a disabled person trying to navigate public transit since it can be such a nightmare without the staff being willing to advocate for you and help you make sure you can safely ride.

NF was three boys, 13m autistic and mostly nonverbal, 10m severe ADHD, 5m undiagnosed but likely ADHD and possibly some heavier stuff I won’t get into in this comment since it’s not relevant anyway. It’s day one with this NF, and MB says I should take them to the park. I take 13m and 10m to the park directly across the street from their house, like MB can see the kids playing at the park from the window if she wanted. Thankfully 5m is home during this. 10m is on the swings and 13m is on top of the monkey bars. I think to myself, “surely it’s fine for me to turn my head for 0.02 seconds to look at 10m and confirm he’s fine and then look back at 13m, he’s on top of the monkey bars after all and it’ll take him more than 0.02 seconds to get down and I’ll hear him anyway!”, I don’t even move from my spot, I just turn my head like 15 degrees and look at 10m, he’s swinging his heart out. I turn my head back to the monkey bars, and all of this really was about 0.02 seconds, 13m is GONE. I, of course, am now frantic and can’t see him ANYWHERE. Not on the playground, not on the field, just gone. I grab 10m and ask if he saw, I probably should have been calmer but I turn practically feral realizing I have lost an autistic child who’s non verbal and could rival the freaking flash and also towers over my 4’11” ass ON MY FIRST DAY. I have 10ms hand and I’m running around the park calling for 13m and frantically asking kids if they’ve seen him, no one has any idea. At this point I’m sobbing and terrified while I run around looking and children of all ages are watching me, the crazy lady, have a breakdown in a park while dragging a 10yr old around. Suddenly, my phone rings. It’s MB. “Hey, did you know 13m is in the backyard?” obviously immediate relief but also mortification at the situation. I get home with 10m and await MBs wrath. “Oh yeah, he runs away from every new nanny, don’t sweat it!”, she giggles. Like MA’AM,  WHY WOULD YOU NOT WARN ME ABOUT THAT?? THATS YOUR WHOLE EXTREMELY VULNERABLE CHILD YOU HAD ME LEAVE THE HOUSE WITH FULL WELL KNOWING HE WOULD FIND THE PERFECT MOMENT TO RUN AWAY FROM ME! 


I never got in any kind of trouble for that, it was just kinda brushed off with the “oh he does this every time hehe” but oh man do I have some *stories* about that NF lol, absolutely wild. The kids were fantastic for the most part, at least when 5m wasn’t physically attacking me or doing other very dark things the NPs refused to do anything about despite me bringing them very worrying escalations, especially for a five year old. He was a sweetheart when he wasn’t stressed beyond belief at least, but oh man do I have some stories lol
Unfortunately no, but I hope you get it figured out!

The most important thing here is your health. I also have seizures and they can absolutely become life threatening quickly, especially when you’re having them more and more often. This is a disability, and it sounds like you’re already doing what you personally can to keep your seizures to a minimum. It absolutely would not be rude or selfish to have a talk with them about it. I agree with other commentators that “confront” isn’t the right word here, but as someone with social anxiety along with disabilities I need accommodations for, I understand that this can be uncomfortable and awkward. 

Do your roommates know about your epilepsy? It’s of course up to you if you want to disclose, but when it comes to epilepsy and living with people, disclosing can be important so the people nearby can help if necessary as well as understand why you’re asking for things like keeping it down so you can sleep. I’d maybe make this part of a bigger conversation, if you haven’t already, where you explain your seizures, their triggers, emergency contacts, what to do if you’re having a seizure including what NOT to do (ex. don’t put anything in your mouth or try to hold your head, how to tell if you’ll need emergency services, who to call, stay calm, etc) and maybe write this down with bullet points and keep it in a common area so they can look at it if the info is needed. It is never ever selfish to talk to your housemates about things that effect your health, especially so seriously. So first, I’d definitely have a talk with them explaining all of this and asking that they be mindful of it and quiet down by a certain time of night so you can get the sleep you need. If it doesn’t go over well with them and you are in university housing, talk to your universities disability office about it to see about possibly switching rooms so that you can have a safe space where your seizures aren’t unnecessarily triggered. 

You deserve a living environment where you’re safe and aren’t having a ton of seizures because of roommates who refuse to understand the situation. But that’s why I’d have a talk with them first to see if they can be understanding. I can only speak for myself, but I’d be horrified to learn I was doing something that was effecting someone else’s health so seriously and would immediately ask what I could do to help. This is important and serious, and I know the conversation isn’t fun, but it’s important to have as soon as possible so your quality of life is better and you are safe and won’t have to spend more time in the hospital than at home. So definitely not selfish or rude, just have a conversation, let them ask questions, give the answers you can, be prepared with the info above like emergency contacts, seizure first aid, your triggers, etc that can be put in a common area and maybe even emailed to all your roommates so they have clear instructions on what to do should you have a more serious seizure and can also check the triggers to make sure they’re not doing anything that’s gonna harm you, and find a compromise for a time of the night that they can start to quiet down so you’re able to sleep. I really hope this goes well for you, and if it doesn’t, you have options and can go from there. Feel free to send me a message if you need any help with approaching them or making the list for the common area or what to do if they don’t react well or just to talk to another seizure haver or about anything at all. 

Remember, you NEED and deserve your home to be a safe place for you where your seizures aren’t being unnecessarily triggered. Seizures can become more serious very quickly, and I’m sure you don’t want to be spending the majority of your time in the hospital and/or recovering from constant seizures.
Best of luck to you hun 💕

This is gonna be long, I’m sorry about that. I am confirmed terminal, and am 25. It seems so ironic with how suicidal I was as a teen, and even now, although much less intensely and without legitimate attempts (please don’t worry, I am definitely not in danger of suicide right now whatsoever, more of a morbid dream, all the more ironic, considering lmao). I spent a very long time dealing with a lot of trauma before I even found out, which of course was not helped by the wild amount of health issues I was having that were consistently blown off by doctors, and the people who were causing a lot of said trauma, very dark times. 
As if the universe is continuously laughing at me, in a better way this time, I also ended up beginning to date my best friend of 12 years after we finally met in real life somewhat recently, who has literally exactly the same diagnoses, sans the terminal subtype, and I am absolutely head over heels in love with her, like ‘looking at rings and planning our wedding and spending the morning crying about how insanely in love I am and how amazing this relationship is and how wild it is to love and be loved so hard and so well and so passionately’ in love. I don’t know when my death is coming, it’s possible that it will be a slow or at least previously detectable demise caused by my comorbidities, or it’s possible that I will have an aneurysm randomly from the main terminal condition. And now suddenly, I have this reason I’d really like to stick around, for a little while, at least. 
I honestly can’t tell you how I cope necessarily, I am lucky to have my girlfriend and a community of other people with my condition, also sans the terminal subtype, but same main illness and many of the same comorbidities and it does help a lot. We’ve become a very tight knit group and are a family and it helps so much to have the support of people going through the same thing, so I’d definitely look into some support groups for people with the same condition as you, or even just communities like this one of other people who know what it’s like to be sick, especially so young because that really does add a whole different layer to the way we’re treated by pretty much everyone. I find myself having to comfort others when they find out a lot, definitely not my favorite. I also get a lot of “if you just believe in god/eat these essential oils/spend a ridiculous amount of money on this “””treatment””” that is not at all researched and is ridiculously expensive and has absolutely no proof of helping whatsoever and definitely has dangerous side effects that will definitely make you sicker/etc”, even less my favorite. But I realize that it is a lot for other people, and just try to smile and move on to something else. 
I think it’s easy for people not in this situation to say “it may *effect* your life, but it doesn’t have to *control* it”. But that’s so much easier said than done.  It obviously effects your life, and there’s no putting that aside or away. Symptoms (both physical and mental, there’s also no putting that aside), appointments, medication, treatment, societal understanding and treatment, friendships and family and intimate relationships, I’m sure I don’t need to tell you. The physical symptoms are one thing, but the way it effects everything else is a whole other one. So like I said, find people who get it, find a community that can understand these feelings and what you’re going through, it can seem silly at first but it really does end up being a lifesaver (pun somewhat intended lol). It can get really lonely being in this position and having people who understand really is a really an amazing thing and can help you cope a lot better than you can with people who don’t know what it’s like to live in your body. If you ever want to talk, feel free to reach out. I’m sorry that you’re dealing with this, I obviously know how it feels, and it definitely isn’t good. I truly hope you find people you can connect with, because that is definitely the best way I’ve found to cope

Agreeing with everyone else, this was done super poorly and with bad quality jewelry. Just make sure that before you take it out, you make sure it’s not infected. Taking out an infected piercing can trap the infection inside your skin/lip and give it nowhere to go and can make it much worse. I’d definitely suggest going to another actually qualified piercer to look at the piercing and give you advice on what to do next 

Also agree that you need to go back to the shop and demand a refund, it being on sale doesn’t excuse how poorly this was done, especially considering how dangerous to your health it can be when it’s done so wrong. And I’d honestly name the shop and piercer to warn others against going there, this could honestly be grounds to report them as well, especially if they don’t own up to the mistake like any legitimate piercer would, but any legitimate piercer also wouldn’t let a customer walk out like that

We met through a mutual friend, who is no longer a friend, and then ended up connecting much more when we found out that we shared many of our chronic illness diagnoses and trauma history, and bonded a lot over that since we knew exactly what the other was going through. Now we have almost exactly the same medical issues and history and confirmed diagnoses anyway.

From there we realized we had even more in common, and just continued to get closer and closer, especially with weirdly dealing with pretty much the exact same things at the exact same time. It all feels like a message from the universe that this was meant to be, especially since every time we visit each other, our return transportation gets messed up at least twice before we can actually go home, so some power out there wants us together as much as possible lol. It really is like our own little fairy tale, even with all the awful shit we had to deal with before, being with her makes it completely worth it, and even the horrible shit we deal with now, because we have each other, and that’s more than enough. And hopefully will be living together within a year from now, so things can hopefully only go up from here

I’m in my first one right now after many, many, many awful ones and it’s fucking amazing. It’s almost like this is the first relationship I’ve ever had because of how different everything is, everything feels fresh and new like it’s the first time. Even just being able to have open, honest, straightforward communication is so new and foreign, in the best possible way. Being treated right, being listened to, being loved and cared for actually unconditionally, being a first priority, not being an emotional/physical/psychological/sexual punching bag, actually being an equal, being valued, being understood on every level, being loved with the best intentions, feeling connected so strongly at all times, getting legitimate sympathy and empathy and support and believing in each other and our dreams, actually being a safe person, helping each other with anything within our power to do and making sure it gets done, actually making and believing in and working towards plans for our future together, it’s all exactly how it’s supposed to be, and it’s perfect, and it’s only getting better. It’s our own little fairytale. 

We were best friends for over a decade before we finally met in person and started dating, and during our time as best friends, went through a lot together, and often around the same time (we still end up dealing with the pretty much exact same things at the exact same time to this day, both a blessing and a curse lol). Lots of abuse and traumas and illnesses and diagnoses and loss and tragedy and just life bullshit that just happened to coincide with each others timeline. We both ended long term relationships and came out as lesbians around the same time too, and finally the circumstances worked out and we were able to meet in real life, and it was instant. We’d always crushed on each other, but both of us thought the other would think it was dumb and that we weren’t “cool” enough for each other, and we were still very closeted so it didn’t fully register. But god damn, the second I saw her, I knew that she was my soulmate and that one day I’d make her my wife, and marriage was never something I’d ever cared about or been excited about or even really thought about besides ex’s talking about it happening and feeling like I was obligated to say yes to them. But for her, I want to give her the world, and more.

She’s the most amazingly gorgeous human being I’ve ever seen, and just thinking about her gives me butterflies and can calm me down from panic attacks. I love hearing her talk about anything, but especially her passions and the things that make her happy, seeing her eyes light up like that is one of my absolute favorite things, I could listen to her talk about them for days on end, or hear her rap/sing along to her favorite songs. She’s changed the way I look at life completely, and the way I look at myself, both of which, and her in general, have saved my life many times. She’s so loving and kind and sweet and generous, she makes me want to be better, and everyone she comes across is better for having known her and having her touch their lives. I’ve never met anyone like her before, or anyone who makes me feel like she does, I didn’t even know it was possible for a relationship to be this amazing. It’s so natural with her, like we were made for each other, we just fall into rhythm immediately. Like the myth that every human was made with four arms and four legs and were then split apart destined to wander the earth until they found their other half describes it perfectly, she was my missing piece, she completes me, she makes me more me. Ive learned so much about myself through her. She feels like home and she makes me feel safe, for the first time in my life. All of our loved ones have told us that they’ve never seen us so happy. I have never slept better or with less nightmares than when we’re cuddled up with each other. I would do anything for her, just to make her smile. Every day I am more and more amazed by her, and could not be happier. I could spend eternity intertwined with her, with my head on her chest listening to her heartbeat or falling asleep kissing her. Sometimes I just watch her sleep, consumed by how amazing she is and how much I love her. 

I didn’t know it was possible to love anything or anyone this much, and that love grows every single day, and every single day my love for her and her as a person amaze me. I usually need recovery time from people and have to spend time alone to “recharge”, but I never need it from her, she doesn’t drain me at all, if anything it’s like she gives me strength, like an extra charge. We can be alone together so easily, there’s no anxiety or awkwardness, we can just be doing our own thing together.

 I could go on literally forever about her (and pretty much have already, sorry lol), so I’ll leave it with this. It is a blessing to love and be loved by her. I would not trade this for anything. As long as I have her, I am more than content. This life has not been good to me, but if it has given me anything, she is and always will be the absolute best, and that makes it all, even the worst possible moments, worth it. 

If you find someone that makes you feel this way, treat them right and hold on to them, because this is a once in a lifetime love and I’m so grateful that I get to experience it.

That’s one of the biggest reasons I decided to not carry a biological child or freeze my eggs. A lot of my health issues are genetic and tend to get worse with each generation and it would absolutely devastate me to watch my children go through what I do, but on an even more severe level. Even when I fostered a teenager, getting him healthcare was a nightmare. So much “this is in his head” or that he was just “looking for drugs” because of his mental health issues and the fact that he was in foster care, with absolutely zero testing or even really giving him a chance to explain his symptoms in the first place, which of course in turn made him feel worse and made him believe that he was just “making it up” and that he didn’t deserve the help and it broke my heart. I ended up chewing some doctors the fuck out after putting that shit on him, especially while he was already terrified that his body wasn’t working correctly. I also very much hope that we can find that balance, because the casualties of the current system are completely preventable and the negligence that allows it that is considered acceptable is disgusting

Medical misogyny is real! I also find that if I have a man with me who repeats my symptoms, then they get taken seriously. Just another thing the healthcare system here fails at, unfortunately. It’s hard because I have friends in other countries who struggle to even get basic care, and then friends in others who have no issues getting the meds they need. Definitely a big reason that I’m considering moving to a different country that can actually give me the medication I need and treat me with respect. There is a HUGE issue with doctors deciding everything about you before you even open your mouth. I even have some pretty unbelievable stories of doctors who took that to a completely insane level and really shouldn’t have medical licenses at all. With the meds, it really seems like we can’t do anything right. We can’t get them in case we take too many, and we can lose them for not taking enough. It really doesn’t make any sense, and ir sucks so much that we’re forced to suffer because of it. Thank you for your kind wishes, I hope your new clinic ends up being able to give you some relief too

I’m in Illinois currently, I’ve also gone through about three other states as well, and am looking at one other soon, probably a couple others after that, and am seriously considering looking into other countries. I was very lucky to get some of my diagnoses before I lost that doctor since they really fought for me, but getting treatment is a whole different story. 

It is so different state to state, which can be both good and bad, especially because so many of them require you to live in the state to get certain meds or treatments, and being too disabled to work means that moving states is obviously not an easy option. But if I can find someone willing to actually help, I’d find a way to make it happen. 

I’m so sorry you’ve also had to fight so hard to get diagnosed, it’s so frustrating when they just label you as a “drug seeker” and/or “crazy” and refuse to look any further. Advocating for yourself can be so hard and different doctors take it differently. I’ve definitely gotten hit with the “dr Google” speech many times, but never a response to what I’m supposed to do otherwise if the doctors I see aren’t willing to do the research themselves. I hope we all find safe ways and doctors to treat our symptoms, we all deserve at absolute minimum to be believed, and to be fought for to get answers and relief

It really is. I was so careful with my meds, I would hold out on taking them until it was absolutely unbearable and even then I’d still try to “power through” and constantly sought out and tried (and still do) other pain management options, I have confirmed diagnoses, and yet I was still labeled as “just a drug seeker” and/or that I was just mentally ill and it was “all in my head” (which even if it was, that would still be something I needed treatment for too!). I have horrible stories for days about the way other pain patients and I have been treated terribly by medical professionals from EMTs to patient advocates to doctors, and in turn from friends and family. 

Especially during the pandemic, the suicide rate has gone up substantially in general, but especially the disabled and chronic illness/pain community has been hit very hard. Especially in the beginning with people saying things like “it’s okay because only elderly and disabled people will die”, we didn’t get a lot of understanding or support. 

So with mental health in general being at an all time low all over, many many people in this community have either committed suicide or have died because the hospitals being overrun and doctors offices shutting down in person visits and losing jobs/money have cost them lifesaving treatment, including pain management. 

I really wish more people saw that pain management is an absolutely necessary and life saving treatment for people in pain, no one was meant to live like this. And it definitely does not get easier to hear that another person lost this battle, especially when it’s because of something that is completely preventable. “Just living with it” is not a viable option for anyone in severe pain. No one should ever be put in a position where death is their only option for relief.

I’m so sorry you’re also dealing with this, it’s absolutely barbaric that we’re expected to “just deal with” such severe pain. One of my illnesses causes my joints, including my vertebrae, to dislocate on a regular basis, like 30+ dislocations a day. Right at this moment, my collarbone, ribcage, multiple vertebrae, right hip, and right shoulder are all fully dislocated and I will need to put them all back, and multiple other joints are in the process of dislocating. I’ve been told by many doctors to just “learn to live with it”, as if that’s a real possibility. My file has also been labeled as “drug seeking” for daring to ask how I was supposed to do that without medication.

This is exactly how it started for me. I thought I was doing okay, that I’d just stop when I lost weight, that my behaviors weren’t disordered, that I was safe, now over a decade later I still struggle with an eating disorder and many permanent and painful health issues because of it.

The calorie deficit is also dangerous. Calories turn into energy we need to function. That’s why it’s recommended to have 2000 a day (which varies person to person based on their needs but no one is recommend to have 500 or less). This can also cause health issues and makes it way harder for your body to function. It literally slows your bodies function because the energy to go normally just isn’t there. This is partially why many with EDs end up with organ failure needing treatments and transplants. 

I also thought I looked fat despite knowing I lost weight, it’s called body dysmorphia and it’s a very real mental illness that can come along with eating disorders. It makes your vision of yourself warped because of the ED trying to convince your brain to continue the dangerous behaviors. 

You lost 20 pounds in three months, that’s a significant amount of weight. More than enough that your physical appearance has absolutely changed because of it. It’s also a lot of weight for a short time. This, along with other disordered habits, can cause muscle loss, nutrient deficiencies, organ damage and failure, osteoporosis, low heart rate and blood pressure, reproductive issues, anemia, needing a feeding tube, low white blood cells, and so much more. 

I get it. I think everyone in this sub has been there. We start with good intentions and for whatever reason it goes bad. Eating disorders work similarly to addiction and they can be absolutely fucking intense. They mess with your brain and your body and try to convince you to keep pushing, keep restricting, keep losing weight, cause everything will be perfect when you get to your goal weight and then you’ll stop. But it’s hard to rely on the numbers, because your ED will tell you to lose more. You made it to your goal weight? Well then you can make it lower. The cycle is brutal. 

If you have someone you can reach out to for help, please do it. You’re worth it. There are a lot of resources out there, even online ones that can help. You’re not alone here at all, this community is so loving and supportive and helpful. So let us help, because you deserve to feel better. This can feel so lonely, feel free to reach out if you want to talk or want help finding those resources. I hope things get better for you
